items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: And the lead trumpet player was ready to kill me. In fact Sid told me that he would kill me if I ever did that again to the band.

ctx.x: When you got on the Woody Herman band was there — were you ready for it and did it fulfill your expectations?

Oh and more. Yeah that was, working for Woody was — well working with both Woody and Kenton were both wonderful experiences, diametrically opposed in musical approaches. But I was ready for both of those bands because I did my homework. But Woody’s band, to me, was like a big small group. The writers that he had were so good. Alan Broadbent, Tony Klatka, and Bill Stapleton. Great charts. And Woody’s willingness for the rhythm section to try new things. You know the album that a lot of people talk about is “Giant…

That’s really interesting because on occasion I’ve asked some musicians who played very, I’ll call it experimental music sometimes free jazz. If they sat down and talked about it first, like okay let’s play without bar lines and this kind of thing, and normally they said no, it just happened. But in this case you’re saying the three of you made a conscious decision to play in a different manner.
